description.summary: the desktop shell's surface roles and system events

protocol.description:
The desktop shell tells the compositor which of its surfaces is the bar, the dock, the switcher and so on, and the compositor tells the shell about the events only it can see: the real modifier keys, modifier gestures, the app switcher, Mission Control's layout, hot corners, edge reveals and the kill chord.
Apps are named by their app key string and windows by their ext_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1 identifier string, because the shell binds this global on a different connection from the one that holds its toplevel handles, and no Wayland object crosses connections.
This protocol is a draft. Until it is declared stable, version 1 may change in place with every client and the server updated together. Version 2 adds, without touching version 1's messages or opcodes, which outputs Mission Control is open on, Space pictures and dropping a window on a Space in Mission Control; every message it adds says `since="2"`. Version 3 adds, again after everything older, a "new desktop" drop target: dropping a window on it makes a Space with the window; every message it adds says `since="3"`. Version 4 adds, again after everything older, the start and the end of a window drag in Mission Control; every message it adds says `since="4"`.

request.name: set_role

description.summary: give a shell surface its role

request.description: `surface` must be a layer surface of this client; anything else raises `bad_surface`. A role held by another live surface raises `role_taken`.

request.name: set_minimise_target

description.summary: where a window minimises to

request.description: The rectangle, local to the dock surface, that the window named by `toplevel` shrinks into when minimised. Replaces an earlier target for that window.

description.summary: forget a window's minimise target

request.name: switcher_pick

description.summary: the person picked an app in the switcher

request.description: `index` is the position the compositor gave in `switcher_app`.

description.summary: the person dismissed the switcher
open or close an overview
move every window aside, or back

request.name: window_menu_pick

description.summary: the person picked an entry of a window's menu

request.description: Answers `window_menu`. An unknown window or entry is ignored; so is an entry the window's state does not offer.

request.name: split_pick

description.summary: the person picked the other half of a Split View

request.description: Answers `split_choose`: `toplevel` is one of the candidates sent after it. A window that is no candidate now, or no choosing, is ignored.

request.name: split_cancel

description.summary: the person turned the choice of a Split View down

request.description: Escape, or a click elsewhere. The first window stays alone, full screen. Without a choosing it is ignored.

request.name: split_divide

description.summary: the divider of a Split View was moved

request.description: `toplevel` is either window of the pair. `share` is the leading (left) window's part of the width, in thousandths; the compositor keeps it between 200 and 800 and holds each half to its window's smallest width. A window that is in no Split View is ignored.

request.name: destroy

description.summary: destroy the object

request.description: Shell surfaces keep their roles until they are destroyed.

event.description: `progress` is in thousandths: 0 closed, 1000 open.

event.name: overview_slot

event.description: Sent for each window; the set is complete at `overview_done`.

event.name: overview_space

event.description: Sent for each Space; the set is complete at `overview_done`.

event.name: overview_done

description.summary: the overview layout is complete

event.description: Ends a batch of `overview_slot` and `overview_space` events.

description.summary: the pointer triggered a hot corner

event.name: reveal

description.summary: an edge reveal changed

event.description: In full screen, the bar or the dock slides in from its edge, or away.

event.name: menu_flash

description.summary: flash a menu title

event.description: A key equivalent of the app ran the menu item at `item`; the bar flashes its menu.

description.summary: an app rang the bell

event.name: reopen

description.summary: an app was activated with no windows

event.description: The shell decides what reopening means for that app.

event.name: window_menu

description.summary: show a window's menu

event.description: The pointer rested on the window's green light, or the window asked for its menu. The shell draws the menu at (`x`, `y`), in global logical pixels, with the entries of `window_entry` in menu order. Bit `n` of `enabled` is set when the entry with code `n` can be picked now; the others are shown dimmed. A pick comes back as `window_menu_pick`; a dismissal sends nothing.

event.name: split_choose

description.summary: offer the other half of a Split View

event.description: `first` went full screen on `side`. The shell offers the windows named by the `split_candidate` events that follow at once, most recently used first, for the other half. The offer lasts until `split_choice_end`; the answer is `split_pick` or `split_cancel`.

event.name: split_candidate

description.summary: a window that can fill the other half

event.description: One per candidate, straight after `split_choose`.

event.name: split_choice_end

description.summary: the choice of a Split View is over

event.description: A pick, a cancel, or `first` left full screen or closed: the shell takes its offer away.

event.name: killed

description.summary: the kill chord was pressed

event.description: Every agent lease has ended.

request.name: get_space_capture_source

description.summary: a picture source for one Space of an output

request.description: Creates an ext_image_capture_source_v1 that shows the Space `space_id` of `output`: its windows where they sit on the output, over a transparent background (the shell draws the wallpaper), scaled to `width` by `height` pixels (the shell's miniature; each side is kept between 1 and 1024). Use it with the standard ext_image_copy_capture_manager_v1; the session's buffer constraints announce that size, and a frame is sent only when something in the Space changed since the last one. The windows are drawn without their frames. A Space that does not exist, or is not on `output`, gives a source whose sessions are stopped at once; so does a Space that is removed while the session lives. Version 2 drew only the Space the output shows now. From version 3 any desktop Space of the output has a picture: the windows of a Space that is not shown are laid out where they would sit if it were shown, for the picture only, and the picture is sent again when one of them changes. A full-screen or Split View Space shows its windows as they sit.

request.name: space_target_clear

description.summary: forget the Space targets of an output

request.description: Removes every rectangle set with `space_target` for `output`. Send it, then the new rectangles, when the shell's Spaces bar changes.

request.name: space_target

description.summary: a place a window can be dropped on a Space

request.description: While a window is dragged in Mission Control, releasing it over this rectangle moves it to the Space `space_id`. The rectangle is in global logical pixels (like `overview_space`). Later targets are in front of earlier ones. An empty rectangle raises `bad_target`. A Space that does not exist is kept but never hit.

request.name: space_target_new

description.summary: the place a window can be dropped to make a new Space

request.description: While a window is dragged in Mission Control, releasing it over this rectangle (the Spaces bar's "add desktop" tile) makes a new Space on `output` and moves the window to it; Mission Control stays open. The rectangle is in global logical pixels, like `space_target`; it is in front of every `space_target` rectangle of the output and there is one per output, a later request replaces it. An empty rectangle removes it (no error). `space_target_clear` leaves it alone.

event.name: overview_output

description.summary: Mission Control is open or closed on an output

event.description: Sent for every output, just before each `overview_state`, and for an output that is plugged in while Mission Control is open. Mission Control follows the Mac's way with separate Spaces on each display: it opens on every output at once, each with its own windows and its own Spaces bar. `shown` is `shown` for an output whose Mission Control is up (entering, open or leaving) and `hidden` when it is closed. The shell draws its Spaces bar on the outputs that are shown only.

event.name: drop_target

description.summary: the dragged window is over a Space target

event.description: While a window is dragged in Mission Control (a press on its slot, then a move past a small distance), the Space target under the pointer changed. `space_id` is the Space of the `space_target` rectangle under the pointer on `output`, or null when none is: the shell highlights it. It is sent with null when the drag ends, by a drop or by the window flying back.

event.name: drop_target_new

description.summary: the dragged window is over the new-Space target

event.description: While a window is dragged in Mission Control, the pointer entered (`shown`) or left (`hidden`) the `space_target_new` rectangle of `output`: the shell highlights the "add desktop" tile. It is sent `hidden` when the drag ends, by a drop or by the window flying back. `drop_target` is sent null for the same output when this one is `shown`.

event.name: window_drag_begin

description.summary: a window drag started in Mission Control

event.description: A press on a window's slot moved past the small distance, so the window is being dragged on `output`: the shell shows which targets (the Spaces of its bar and the "add desktop" tile) accept it. `drop_target` and `drop_target_new` follow while the pointer moves. One drag at a time; it ends with `window_drag_end`.

event.name: window_drag_end

description.summary: the window drag in Mission Control is over

event.description: The window was released or the drag was abandoned. `outcome` says where it went. It comes after the `drop_target` and `drop_target_new` messages that clear the highlight.
